needs.label: Developmental or intellectual disability (including Down syndrome)

glossary.plain: Testing to see if your child has a delay or disability and what help they need. Early intervention and public schools do this for free.
Free help for children under 3, usually at home, such as speech or physical therapy and coaching for parents.
A written school plan for a child who needs special education. It lists goals, services such as speech therapy, and supports. Parents are part of the team that writes it.

A written school plan for a child with a disability who does not need special education but needs changes to learn, such as extra test time or breaks. A child who does not qualify for an IEP may still get a 504 plan.
A therapy often used for autism that teaches skills step by step. Insurance, Medicaid and TRICARE rules for it vary.
In Ohio, the county office for developmental disabilities. It decides who qualifies and helps plan and pay for services.
A Medicaid program that pays for help at home and in the community, such as aides or respite, for people who qualify.
Supplemental Security Income: monthly payments from Social Security for people with disabilities who have low income and savings.
A savings account for a person with a disability that does not count against SSI or Medicaid limits.
A court gives another adult the right to make decisions for a person 18 or older. It removes some of that person's rights, so less restrictive options are worth looking at first.
The young adult keeps their rights and chooses trusted people to help them understand choices and make decisions.
The part of an IEP, starting by age 14 in Ohio, that plans for life after high school: work, school and living.
Short-term care that gives family caregivers a break.
The military's Exceptional Family Member Program for active duty families with special medical or school needs.
Mobile Response and Stabilization Services: Ohio's free youth crisis teams. Call or text 988 and ask for MRSS.

attribution: Disability and neurodiversity listings are adapted from the family guide in the Veteran Resident Resource Guide, created by Travis Vought and shared by Veteran Home Guardians (CC BY 4.0).

resources.name: National Domestic Violence Hotline
resources.what: Free, private support any hour of the day. An advocate can help you think through safety, shelter and next steps, whether or not you are ready to leave.
resources.how: Call, text or chat. You do not have to give your name.

resources.name: Find your local domestic violence program
resources.what: ODVN connects you to the domestic violence program that serves your county. Local programs offer shelter, safety planning, court advocates and support groups. Shelter addresses are kept private for safety.
resources.how: Call the information and referral line, or use the "Get Help Now" list on the ODVN website to find your county program.

resources.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
resources.what: Free support for anyone in emotional distress or crisis, any hour. In Ohio you can also ask 988 for a youth mobile crisis team for a child or teen.

resources.name: Ohio Sexual Violence Helpline
resources.org: Ohio Alliance to End Sexual Violence
resources.what: Confidential support and advocacy for survivors of sexual violence anywhere in Ohio, any hour.

resources.name: Protection orders: free form helper
resources.what: A civil protection order is a court order telling an abuser to stay away. This free tool asks plain questions and fills in the Ohio court forms for you. Filing has risks, so talk with an advocate about a safety plan first.
resources.how: Use the form helper on a safe device. You do not need a lawyer to file, but legal aid may represent you for free.

resources.name: Ohio 211
resources.what: One number for local help with food, housing, utilities, health care and other needs. Open 24 hours a day.
resources.how: Dial 211 and say what you need and what county you are in.

resources.name: Find homeless services and shelter in your county
resources.org: Coalition on Homelessness and Housing in Ohio (COHHIO)
resources.what: Each Ohio county has one front door for shelter and housing help. COHHIO lists the right number to call for every county.
resources.how: Open the Ohio housing resource guide and choose your county. If you are fleeing abuse, call a domestic violence program first.

resources.name: Help with heating and electric bills (HEAP)
resources.what: HEAP helps households at or below 175% of the federal poverty level pay utility bills. Crisis programs can help when you have a shutoff notice.
resources.how: Apply online, or call to be connected to your local energy assistance provider.

resources.name: Food, cash and Medicaid: one application
resources.what: One application covers SNAP (food), Ohio Works First cash assistance, Medicaid and child care help. Your county Job and Family Services office decides eligibility.
resources.how: Apply online or by phone. Fill in as much as you can; you can add documents later.

resources.name: WIC: food for pregnancy, babies and children under 5
resources.what: WIC provides healthy food, formula help, breastfeeding support and health screenings for pregnant and postpartum women, infants and children up to age 5.
resources.how: Call the Help Me Grow helpline to find your county WIC clinic and make an appointment.

resources.name: Help paying for child care
resources.org: Ohio Department of Children and Youth
resources.what: Publicly Funded Child Care helps working or in-school parents pay for licensed child care. Families generally qualify at or below 145% of the federal poverty level.
resources.how: Apply through the same Ohio Benefits application used for food and Medicaid, online or by phone.

resources.name: Child support: open or change a case
resources.what: Your county Child Support Enforcement Agency can establish paternity, set up a support order, collect payments and review an order when circumstances change.
resources.how: Start on the state child support website or call the customer service line to reach your county agency.

resources.name: Free legal help: custody, divorce, eviction, benefits
resources.org: Ohio Legal Help and Ohio legal aid
resources.what: Plain-language legal information and court forms, plus a connection to the free legal aid office for your county.
resources.how: Search your topic on the website, or call to reach the legal aid office that serves your area.
